artists.biography:
Mojave 3 were a British rock band formed in the wake of Slowdive’s breakup in 1995, bringing together Neil Halstead, Rachel Goswell, and Ian McCutcheon before later adding keyboardist Alan Forrester and guitarist Simon Rowe. The group emerged from the shoegaze world but quickly moved toward a softer, more atmospheric style shaped by dream pop, slowcore, folk, and acoustic textures.

Their debut album, Ask Me Tomorrow, arrived in 1996 on 4AD and set the tone for a run of records that included Out of Tune, Excuses for Travellers, Spoon and Rafter, and Puzzles Like You. Mojave 3 became known for their restrained, melancholy songwriting and their ability to translate the emotional haze of shoegaze into a more spacious, roots-leaning sound, earning a loyal following and critical respect for their subtle evolution.

After releasing five albums, the band went on hiatus in 2007, returned for live dates in 2011, and later effectively ended when Halstead and Goswell reformed Slowdive.

lastfm.wiki_content: Ask Me Tomorrow is the debut album by Mojave 3, released by 4AD on 16 October 1995 in the UK and on 16 January 1996 in the US. The album was released roughly eight months after the release of Pygmalion, the third studio album by Mojave 3 founders Neil Halstead, Rachel Goswell, and Ian McCutcheon's previous band Slowdive. Musically, the album incorporates elements of alt-country, dream pop, and slowcore. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Ask Me Tomorrow is the debut album by Mojave 3, released on 4AD in 1995. It marked a striking departure from the band members’ Slowdive background, replacing shoegaze density with a hushed, acoustic style shaped by folk, country, and slowcore influences.

The album’s sound is intimate and unhurried, built around Neil Halstead and Rachel Goswell’s understated vocals, gentle guitars, and sparse percussion. Its songs have been described as melancholy but warmly melodic, with a dreamy, desolate atmosphere that recalls alt-country and classic singer-songwriter traditions while retaining a distinctly ethereal quality.

At just nine tracks and a little over 41 minutes, Ask Me Tomorrow became a defining statement for Mojave 3 and a fan favorite. Its restrained, reflective mood and lyrical openness helped establish the band’s identity beyond Slowdive, and it remains one of 4AD’s notable mid-1990s releases.
